column1: # A.8: every tool read of .githooks/pre-push, one row per read, and the prose of the header block generated from it. TAB-separated.
# A prose row: prose, the paragraph it belongs to (bound, own, lists; rows of one paragraph are joined in order), its text.
# A read row: kind, read, fact, case, key, class, short, end.
#   kind   gate= or own= (a judged_read tag, matched to the hook's tags by name) or outside (a read the census finds outside judged_read).

#   fact   the sibling fact that shows a whole answer, and after "Its end:" how an answer cut short is told from a whole one, or why an empty or cut-short exit-0 answer there refuses or publishes nothing: an own= row, and a gate= row whose reason is the safe side, begins "safe:"; an outside row names the report or advice line it serves (or, for the scanner's argument list, the log the scanner run is judged from).

#   case   <file>:<@test title substring>, one match in tests/pre-push-<file>.bats: the case that drives THIS read with a silent tool keyed on its own shape through a real push, asserts the tool fired, then asserts the refusal or the unpublished remote the fact claims.

#   key    an outside row's fixed substring of its read's own command line, matched to exactly one read the census finds outside judged_read (and each such read to exactly one key); - for a gate= or own= row.
#   class  the fact's kind (marker, count, size, listing, digits, status, answer) or the safe reason's (strict, join, backstop, transfer, disarm, probe, report).

#   short  <file>:<@test title substring>, one match: the case that drives THIS read with its real answer CUT SHORT, exit 0, keyed on its own shape, through a real push, asserts the cut shim fired (fired_short), then asserts what the end claims; or, on a gate= or own= row alone, "none:" and the reason no cut applies (an outside row names its case: a cut of a read made for the report can change what the report says, round 8c).
#   end    how the answer's END is bounded: tail, count, size, digits, whole, terminator, verdict, join, fewer, bytes, emptiness, backstop, prefix, status, discarded, report.
# The header block between the hook's two marker lines is GENERATED from this file (tests/pre-push-reads-header.sh): edit this table, never those lines.

column2: bound
column3: The bound of each sibling fact, stated once: a fact that bounds an answer's START (a head marker, a non-empty answer, the first word naming the object, an emptiness compared with a size) says nothing of its END, so each read's line below states both, and its row in tests/pre-push-reads.tsv names a case that cuts the real answer short, exit 0, through a real push, or the reason no cut applies (round 8b3: the commit listing cut to its tip, the added lines to their marker, the addresses inside the committed address, a symlink target to ten bytes, the symlink listing inside a link's mode, the -z listing inside a hidden file's record and the repository root to a main clone's path each published through a real push while its row stated a fact, and two reads whose own= rows said safe published too: an awk silent on the scanner log's ERR line, a credential beside a scanner that counted a commit whole with its credential file unread, and the chosen addresses under an answer cut to a prefix of one, a commit stamped under a banned domain; the r8b2 audit and round 8b3, 2026-09-23).

column2: bound
column3: The END is held by a TAIL marker the read asks for after its answer (the message and address logs, the diff's second --stdin line, the root's work-tree line), by a count or a byte count read apart (the commit count, a size, a count the tool records), by a terminator each item needs (a NUL, the newline after an address, the tab that ends a listing entry's size column), by equality with a whole name or word, or by a verdict any answer under exit 0 gives already; a cut digit run is another number, so a count compared with an independent one bounds itself.

column2: bound
column3: And a read whose answer is its STATUS alone gates nothing where exit 0 is the PERMISSIVE verdict, since a silent tool exits 0: the chosen-address match runs no tool since round 8, and the ancestry of a pushed commit is read since round 8b2 as the commit git merge-base names, which must be the commit the pushed object peels to, read apart and judged a whole name since round 9a (under --is-ancestor a git silent on it and on the commit listing published a middle commit's banned line through a real push of a ref update; 2026-09-23).

column2: own
column3: What stays own=, and why a tool silent there publishes nothing by itself: a read whose empty answer is the object's own, with no sibling fact to hold it against. Each such read's line below says why an empty or cut-short exit-0 answer there refuses or publishes nothing, and its row in tests/pre-push-reads.tsv names the case that shows it with the tool silent through a real push and the case that shows it with the answer cut short, or why no cut applies.

column2: own
column3: The greps among them answer by their status alone (-q), and there exit 0 is the hit, the strict side; the chosen-address MATCH was a third such grep until round 8, where exit 0 was the PERMISSIVE verdict and a grep silent with exit 0 made every stamped address chosen, publishing a banned-domain stamp through a real push (the round 7 refuter, 2026-09-23).

column2: own
column3: A join over the scratch listings disarms one gate on another read when a tool is silent there, while the read it gates stands under its status and its other gates; two tools silent at once, a listing and its gate, are outside this guarantee.

column2: lists
